output.summary: A woody climbing vine native to woodlands in Japan, the Korean peninsula and Sakhalin. It climbs with small aerial roots and produces flat summer flower clusters with peripheral sterile white flowers around numerous fertile off-white flowers. Its young leaves are edible when cooked and are sometimes added to miso in Japan.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten cooked, sometimes in Japanese miso, and are described as tasting like cucumber.
